t: Section 1265, Revised Statutes (10 U. S. C. 841); the last paragraph appearing under the heading “Mileage”, Act of May 28, 1924 (ch. 203, 43 Stat. 202), and the last paragraph appearing tinder the heading “Mileage”, Act of February 11, 1925 (ch. 209, 43 Stat. 879; 34 U. S. C. 871), are hereby repealed.

fable.w: This section only repeals earlier statutory provisions concerning mileage. It sets up no consultation, hearing, advisory body, rulemaking, or right to sue involving any party outside the federal government, so there is nothing that could be read as participation.

qwen_block.w: This section is a repealer clause that removes existing statutory provisions regarding mileage allowances. It does not establish any process for consultation, coordination, or participation with outside parties. It simply changes the legal code by deleting text.
qwen_block.s: Section 1265, Revised Statutes (10 U. S. S. C. 871), are hereby repealed.

opus.w: This provision repeals earlier statutory provisions about mileage. It does not involve anyone outside the federal government in a federal decision, and it creates no hearing, comment period, rulemaking, advisory body or right to sue. Mentions of an 'Act' and a 'heading' are just citations, not any process for outside parties to take part.
opus.b: This section only repeals earlier statutes about mileage. The words "Act" and "heading" might look like they point to some process, but nothing here involves anyone outside the federal government in a decision. There is no consultation, hearing, comment period, advisory body, rulemaking authority or right to sue.

qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might look for hidden procedural requirements in the repealed statutes, but the text provided only states that certain statutes are repealed. The repeal itself is a legislative act, not a participatory process defined in the section.
